sections.title: Pendahuluan Pemeriksaan Neurologis

content.text: The neurological examination follows a systematic approach to localize lesions within the nervous system. Components include: mental status, cranial nerves, motor system (inspection, tone, power, bulk), sensory system (modalities, dermatomes), coordination, gait and stance, and reflexes (deep tendon, superficial, pathological). The examination should always be interpreted in the context of the history.

sections.title: Pemeriksaan Saraf Kranialis

content.text: CN I (Olfactory): smell test with coffee, vanilla, alcohol. CN II (Optic): visual acuity (Snellen chart), visual fields (confrontation), fundoscopy (disc, vessels, macula). CN III, IV, VI (Oculomotor, Trochlear, Abducens): pupil size/shape/reaction (RAPD), extraocular movements (H pattern), nystagmus. CN V (Trigeminal): facial sensation (V1, V2, V3), corneal reflex, masseter/temporalis power, jaw jerk. CN VII (Facial): facial symmetry at rest and with movement (forehead wrinkling, eye closure, smile), taste anterior 2/3 tongue. CN VIII (Vestibulocochlear): hearing (Rinne, Weber), balance. CN IX, X (Glossopharyngeal, Vagus): gag reflex, palatal elevation, voice quality, swallowing. CN XI (Accessory): SCM and trapezius strength. CN XII (Hypoglossal): tongue symmetry, fasciculations, deviation on protrusion.
UMN facial lesion: forehead spared (bilateral innervation); LMN facial lesion: entire face affected including forehead

sections.title: Pemeriksaan Motorik

content.text: INSPECTION: posture, involuntary movements (tremor, chorea, dystonia, fasciculations), muscle wasting, deformities. TONE: assess resistance to passive movement throughout ROM; hypertonia (spasticity, rigidity) vs hypotonia vs paratonia. STRENGTH: MRC grading 0-5 (0=no contraction, 1=flicker, 2=active movement with gravity eliminated, 3=active movement against gravity, 4=active movement against resistance, 5=normal power). BULK: measure limb circumference, compare sides. UMN vs LMN SIGNS: UMN - spasticity, increased reflexes, Babinski positive, no fasciculations, no atrophy; LMN - flaccidity, decreased/absent reflexes, fasciculations, atrophy.

sections.title: Sensorik, Koordinasi, dan Refleks

content.text: SENSORY EXAMINATION: Test primary modalities - light touch, pinprick (pain), temperature, vibration (128 Hz tuning fork), joint position sense. Compare symmetrical points. Map deficits to dermatomes or peripheral nerve territories. COORDINATION: Finger-to-nose test (upper limb), heel-to-shin test (lower limb), rapid alternating movements (dysdiadochokinesia), fine finger movements. Romberg test (proprioception/vestibular function). REFLEXES: Deep tendon reflexes (biceps C5-6, triceps C6-7, supinator C5-6, knee L3-4, ankle S1-2) graded 0-4+. Pathological reflexes: Babinski (UPST, dorsiflexion great toe), Hoffmann, clonus. Primitive reflexes: glabellar, snout, palmomental, grasp. MENINGEAL SIGNS: neck stiffness (nuchal rigidity), Kernig sign, Brudzinski sign.
Sensorik: sentuhan halus, nyeri, suhu, vibrasi, propriosepsi
Tanda meningeal: kaku kuduk, Kernig, Brudzinski
Babinski sign (extensor plantar response) is the most reliable indicator of UMN pathology

sections.title: Gait dan Dokumentasi

content.text: GAIT EXAMINATION: Observe patient walking (heel walking, toe walking, tandem gait). Assess initiation, stride length, arm swing, turning, stability. DOCUMENTATION: Record all findings systematically using standardized formats. Common scales: Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) for consciousness, NIH Stroke Scale (NIHSS) for stroke severity, Modified Rankin Scale (mRS) for disability.
Gait: inisiasi, panjang langkah, ayunan lengan, stabilitas
